summary: Service-object family recovered from the 0x0075A4DC vtable pair: a 0x478-byte owner that holds a kernel handle, a buffered two-word service id, an owner/handle release pair and two embedded sub-objects (a 0x007804BC object at +0x20 and a Text_NgWord content state at +0x30); the batch also merges the separate 8-byte vtable-0x00780EAC handle wrapper whose Create*/Get*Checked helpers are listed here.
evidence: Vtable 0x0075A4DC slots are maybe_Svc_Object_Shutdown (0x001DC080) and maybe_Svc_Object_Delete (0x001DC070). The owner layout is read straight out of 0x001DC080: svcCloseHandle on +4, buffered id at +8/+0xC flushed by Svc_Ipc_Send080E0080 in maybe_Svc_Object_Dtor (0x00505688), owner pointer +0x18 with handle +0x1C, embedded vtable 0x007804BC at +0x20 (same head as maybe_Gfx_MoviePlayer_Dtor 0x001DBFFC), embedded Text_NgWord at +0x30 closed by Text_NgWord_CloseService (0x00515058), -1 at +0x46C and a freed buffer at +0x474. The 8-byte wrapper (vtable 0x00780EAC, handle +4) from Svc_Object_CreateBare/CreateFromDescriptor/GetHandleChecked is a different allocation and only shares the cluster by name.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_Object_Shutdown stores vtable 0x0075A4DC; its slots 0/1 are 0x001DC080 and 0x001DC070.

fields.name: kernelHandle
fields.evidence: Closed with svc 0x23 (svcCloseHandle) and zeroed in maybe_Svc_Object_Shutdown and Svc_Object_ReleaseHandleSlot; Svc_Object_GetHandleChecked asserts it is non-zero before any IPC use.

fields.name: pendingIdLow
fields.evidence: First of the two words flushed through Svc_Ipc_Send080E0080 by maybe_Svc_Object_Dtor when either word is non-zero; forwarded as the first request word by Svc_Object_Cmd1 (0x00505364) and Svc_Object_Cmd3 (0x005052B8).

fields.name: pendingIdHigh
fields.evidence: Second word of the same buffered id: maybe_Svc_Object_Dtor sends it as the second payload word, Svc_Object_Cmd1/Cmd3 pass object+0xC as the trailing request word.

fields.name: maybe_ownerObject
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_Object_Shutdown calls (**(code**)(*self[6] + 4))(self[6], self[7]) then clears self[7]: a parent object whose second vtable slot releases the handle in self[7].

fields.name: ownedHandle
fields.evidence: self[7]: passed as the argument of the owner's release slot (+4) and set to 0 immediately afterwards in maybe_Svc_Object_Shutdown.

fields.name: subObjectVtable
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_Object_Shutdown writes vtable 0x007804BC at self[8]; the same vtable is the main vtable restored by maybe_Gfx_MoviePlayer_Dtor (0x001DBFFC), i.e. an embedded sub-object starts at +0x20.

fields.name: ngWordStateVtable
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_Object_Shutdown writes 0x0078112C at self[0xC] and then calls Text_NgWord_CloseService(self+0xC); Text_NgWord (type TextNgWord, 52 bytes) is a Svc_ContentObject-derived state with fields from +0x18, so its vtable sits at +0x30 here.

fields.name: ngWordWorkBuffer
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_Object_Shutdown calls func_005099F8(self+0xD); Text_NgWord_CloseService does exactly the same on state+4, so +0x34 is the NG-word work buffer that CloseService releases.

fields.name: unknown_0xc0
fields.evidence: PHANTOM offset: struct_db read the vtable slot expression (**(code**)(*piVar2 + 0x30))(piVar2) in Svc_Object_CreateFromDescriptor/CreateWithPayload as array element param_1[0x30]. No code reads a field at 0xC0; emitted only because the batch lists the offset.

fields.name: unknown_0xd0
fields.evidence: PHANTOM offset: struct_db read the vtable slot (**(code**)(*param_1 + 0x34))(param_1) in Svc_Object_Destroy/Release/ReleaseRef/ReleaseRefB as param_1[0x34]. No field at 0xD0 exists.

fields.name: maybe_currentEntryIndex
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_Object_Shutdown stores -1 at self[0x11B]; the sibling object torn down at 0x001DBFFC stores the same -1 in its own current-entry word, i.e. an 'invalid index' sentinel.

fields.name: freedBuffer
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_Object_Shutdown frees self[0x11D] with func_0010F69C and zeroes it; maybe_Gfx_MoviePlayer_Dtor frees its equivalent read-request block at +0x454 the same way.

summary: Handle bundle that owns seven 3DS kernel handles plus an embedded OsHandleBlock: three sibling destructors close every handle with svcCloseHandle (svc 0x23); most likely the thread/event/semaphore bundle used by the icon-cache/content worker.
evidence: maybe_Svc_SyncObject_DestroyC (0x0050F0F8) unlinks the embedded OsHandleBlock at +0x2C through Os_CloseHandleAndUnlink (0x00111E44) and then closes the six handles at +0x00/+0x08/+0x10/+0x1C/+0x24/+0x40; maybe_Svc_SyncObject_DestroyA (0x00509A20) and DestroyB (0x00509B40) are the smaller variant that only owns +0x14 (the sibling is waited on by the icon-cache code around 0x0050A714).

fields.name: kernelHandle0
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_SyncObject_DestroyC: if (*self != 0) svc 0x23; *self = 0.

fields.name: kernelHandle1
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_SyncObject_DestroyC: self[2] closed with svc 0x23 and cleared.

fields.name: kernelHandle2
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_SyncObject_DestroyC: self[4] closed with svc 0x23 and cleared.

fields.name: kernelHandle3
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_SyncObject_DestroyA/B and DestroyC all close the word at +0x14 with svc 0x23 (this is the only handle of the smaller A/B object).

fields.name: kernelHandle4
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_SyncObject_DestroyC: self[7] closed with svc 0x23 and cleared.

fields.name: kernelHandle5
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_SyncObject_DestroyC: self[9] closed with svc 0x23 and cleared.

fields.name: handleBlock
fields.evidence: Os_CloseHandleAndUnlink(self+0xB) = the embedded OsHandleBlock at +0x2C: it carries the list link and its own handle at block+0x14, unlinked and cancelled before the plain handle sweep.

fields.name: kernelHandle6
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_SyncObject_DestroyC: self[0x10] closed with svc 0x23 and cleared.

summary: Loaded icon-cache block archive: a 0x70-byte header, 16 inline 0xC-byte block entries at +0x70..+0x130, a u8 block count, then an out-of-line payload and a 0x20-byte trailer; the same object also caches the parsed index pointers (header, name pool, 0x3C-byte record array) used by the name lookup.
evidence: maybe_Svc_Blob_Serialize (0x00658B28, called by Ui_IconCache_WorkerThread 0x004121B4) copies 0x70 bytes, walks blob->f_130 entries of 0xC bytes at +0x70 (size at +4, data pointer at +8, 4-byte padded), then copies payload(+0x138, size +0x134) and the 0x20-byte trailer at +0x13C. maybe_Svc_Blob_FindRecordByName (0x0065945C) reads the record count from (*(self+0xC))+8, the name strings from +0x10 and the 0x3C-byte record array at +0x18.

fields.name: indexHeader
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_Blob_FindRecordByName loops while i < *(int *)(*(int *)(self + 0xC) + 8): +0xC points at a header whose +8 is the record count.

fields.name: namePool
fields.evidence: Record name = self->f_10 + record->f_8, compared with func_0010540C in maybe_Svc_Blob_FindRecordByName; base of the UTF-8 name strings.

fields.name: recordArray
fields.evidence: Record i = *(int *)(*(int *)(self + 0x18) + i*0x3C); record+8 is the offset of its name in namePool, so +0x18 is an array of 0x3C-byte descriptors.

fields.name: blockCount
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_Blob_Serialize: count = blob->f_130, then i < count blocks are written; 16 block slots of 0xC bytes at +0x70..+0x130 bound the value.

fields.name: payloadSize
fields.evidence: maybe_Svc_Blob_Serialize copies blob->f_134 bytes from +0x138 and advances dst by the same amount.

fields.name: payloadData
fields.evidence: Source pointer of the main payload memcpy (func_00116A14(dst, blob->f_138, blob->f_134)) in maybe_Svc_Blob_Serialize.

fields.name: trailerData
fields.evidence: Non-null blob->f_13C gets a fixed 0x20-byte memcpy as the last step of maybe_Svc_Blob_Serialize.

summary: Per-frame update template shared by UI windows (recovered here from the 24-slot variant 0x00316250): calls the shared core virtual at +0x98 slot +0x2C, advances a 1/30 s clock (+0x124 float, +0x128 frame ticks), runs the due timer entry from the slot array at +0x11C through the member-function adjustor table at +0x13C, and clears a UI mode word when the stop byte at +0x540 is set.
evidence: Svc_TimerSub_RunDue_24 (0x00316250, vtable 0x00763034 slot 1) and maybe_Ui_DungeonWindow_Update (0x002E9614, vtable 0x00782A08) are the same template with 24 and 5 slots; the 1/30 s constant is 0x3D088889, slot index limit 0x18, entry stride 0x18 with callback at +0x34 and adjustor word at +0x38, adjustor base at +0x13C, and Ui_GetCore()->u16_94 is zeroed when +0x540 is set.

fields.name: maybe_coreObject
fields.evidence: (**(code**)(*(int *)(param_1 + 0x98) + 0x2C))() runs the base update; +0x98 is the shared +0x98 object slot of nearly every Ui window class, but this template passes no 'this', so the exact owner is unproven.

fields.name: timerSlots
fields.evidence: Address-taken twice: as a virtual object ((**(code**)(*(int *)(param_1+0x11C)+0x10))(param_1+0x11C), a clock/stop query) and as the base of the 0x18-byte timer entries (param_1 + 0x11C + index*0x18).

fields.name: timerIndex
fields.evidence: Bounded by 0x18 (24 slots) and used as the entry index: param_1 + 0x11C + *(uint*)(param_1 + 0x120) * 0x18.

fields.name: elapsedSeconds
fields.evidence: Accumulated once per frame with the 1/30 s constant 0x3D088889: *(float*)(param_1+0x124) += fVar4.

fields.name: frameTicks
fields.evidence: Integer counter incremented in the same clock block: *(int*)(param_1+0x128) = *(int*)(param_1+0x128) + 1.

fields.name: callbackAdjustorTable
fields.evidence: piVar2 = (int *)(*(int*)(param_1+0x13C) + ((int)entry->f_38 >> 1)); a set bit 0 in +0x38 makes the callback a member-function pointer whose adjustor is read from this table.

fields.name: stopUiModeFlag
fields.evidence: When +0x540 is non-zero the updater zeroes the u16 at Ui_GetCore()->+0x94 (mode/state word) and clears the byte; i.e. a request to drop the UI mode on the next tick.

summary: Archive mount record used by Fs_Archive_OpenRecordByPath: an embedded 0x28-byte archive directory table at +0x20, the matching 0x28-byte file table at +0x48, a base data offset, and a block pool for the 0x30-byte archive accessor nodes; the generated Svc_ prefix is wrong (this is plain fs code).
evidence: maybe_Fs_Archive_OpenRecordByPath (0x00504AE0) passes &self->f_20 to Fs_Archive_ResolvePath (0x00711AD0), &self->f_48 to Fs_Archive_FindFile (0x007118CC) and &self->f_b8 to Mem_PoolAllocNode (0x0011CAB4) for the 0x30-byte nodes of vtable 0x00780E18; Fs_Archive_FindFile's own doc states the file table is 'exactly 0x28 bytes after' the directory table at &mount->f_20.

fields.name: directoryTable
fields.evidence: &self->f_20 is the ArchiveDirTable* of Fs_Archive_ResolvePath; the 0x28-byte table occupies +0x20..+0x48, its next sibling is the file table. Typed u32 only because ArchiveDirTable is not a registered structs.json type.

fields.name: fileTable
fields.evidence: &self->f_48 is the ArchiveFileTable* of Fs_Archive_FindFile (bucket array, 0x20-byte file entries); the file table starts exactly 0x28 bytes after the directory table.

fields.name: baseOffset
fields.evidence: self->f_b0 is added to the resolved entry offset when the accessor node is filled: piVar6[2] = self->f_b0 + entryOffset (maybe_Fs_Archive_OpenRecordByPath).

fields.name: accessorPool
fields.evidence: Mem_PoolAllocNode(&self->f_b8) allocates the 0x30-byte accessor node (vtable 0x00780E18) returned to the caller; +0xB8 is an embedded block pool, not a scalar.

summary: Two-table entry-count pair read by the icon-cache index writer: table 0 selects the count at +0x210, table 1 the count at +0x3C0; each count bounds the loop that appends 8-byte timestamp records for that table's entries to the cache index file.
evidence: Ui_IconCache_WriteIndexTable (0x00658618) picks index->f_210 for table==0 and index->f_3C0 otherwise, then calls func_00658548(index, table, i) per entry and writes its timestamp (or 'ERROR   ') via func_001009DC; called from Ui_IconCache_Commit/Ui_IconCache_FetchIcon's worker. The Svc_ name is inherited from the first pass; the object is the in-memory icon-cache index, not a service.

fields.name: table0Count
fields.evidence: index->f_210 is the loop bound when Ui_IconCache_WriteIndexTable is called with table == 0.

fields.name: table1Count
fields.evidence: index->f_3C0 is the loop bound when Ui_IconCache_WriteIndexTable is called with table != 0 (table 1).

summary: Not a standalone object: the only batch access is Sound_Handle_IsStale reading SoundPlayer+0x74. Sound_Player (type SoundPlayer, 648 bytes) already exists in structs.json, so this record should be folded into that class by a later merge.
evidence: Sound_Handle_IsStale (0x006307A4) is called by Sound_Emitter_UpdateVoices, Sound_SequencePlayer_UpdateVoices, Sound_GetOrAddSlot, Ui_Cue_Finish and Ui_RecipeInfo_IsUnlocked with the Sound_GetPlayer() singleton as self; the three functions clustered here also include a plain interface get/set (0x002BD89C) and an unrelated handle-object dtor (0x001C3858), so the class is a name-based fragment.

fields.name: soundHandleTable
fields.evidence: func_00711090(self+0x74, handle & 0xFFF) resolves a 0xE------- sound handle's low 12 bits to a {payload, fullHandle} entry; the lookup fails (or the stored handle/payload mismatches) => the handle is stale.
